home.title: Ouroboros
home.subtitle: OpenAPI 3.1.0-based REST API Specification Management & Mock Server Library

apiSpec.title: API Specification Management
apiSpec.desc: Create and manage REST API specifications compliant with OpenAPI 3.1.0 standard, and synchronize them with actual implementation.

mockServer.title: Automatic Mock Server
mockServer.desc: Mock APIs are generated immediately upon specification creation, eliminating the need for frontend developers to wait for backend.

validation.title: Implementation Validation
validation.desc: Automatically verify consistency between specifications and implementation using @ApiState annotation.

try.title: Try Feature
try.desc: Track API execution and automatically detect performance issues using OpenTelemetry-based performance tracking and analysis.

websocket.title: WebSocket/STOMP API Management
websocket.desc: Provides WebSocket/STOMP API specification management and code scanning features supporting AsyncAPI 3.0.0 standard.

quickStart.title: Quick Start
quickStart.warning: Note: Ouroboros only supports Spring Boot 3.5.7 and below. It does not work with Spring Boot 4.0.0. See known issues for details.

step1.title: 1. Add Dependencies
step1.versionWarning: ⚠️ Do not use version 1.0.2 as it causes errors. Please use version 1.0.5.

step2.title: 2. Configuration (application.yml)
step2.springwolfNote: ⚠️ Important: The springwolf.enabled=false setting is required even when using REST API only. Without this setting, the application may fail to boot properly.

quickStart.homeConfigCode:
ouroboros:
  enabled: true  # Default: true
  server:
    url: http://localhost:8080
    description: Local Development Server

# Springwolf Configuration (Required)
# Set to false if using REST API only or if WebSocket code scanning is not needed
springwolf:
  enabled: false  # Required when not using WebSocket code scanning

webUI.title: Web UI Overview
webUI.desc: Ouroboros provides an intuitive web-based interface. All operations can be performed through the GUI without writing code.
webUI.desc2: The interface consists of three main areas: sidebar (navigation), main content area (viewing and editing specifications), and action panel (testing and validation).

items.1: Left Sidebar: Navigate all API endpoints, schemas, and WebSocket operations
items.2: Main Content Area: View and edit API specifications, schemas, and messages
items.3: Action Panel: API testing, validation results, and performance analysis

badges.title: Status Badges
badges.desc: The sidebar displays all API endpoints with status badges to see development status at a glance:

items.completed: 🟢 Completed: API is fully implemented and tested
items.implementing: 🟡 Implementing: API is currently under development
items.mock: 🔴 Mock: API exists only as specification (not yet implemented)
items.bugfix: 🟠 Bugfix: API is being fixed for bugs

items.1: Schemas Tab: Create schemas and specify required fields
items.2: APIs Tab: Set Path, Method, then configure Request Body, Response, and Headers via forms
items.3: Import/Export: Import or export OpenAPI files using the "Import YAML" and "Export YAML" buttons in the top right
items.4: API Try Panel: Enter parameters in the "API Try" tab on the API detail screen and click "RUN" to immediately check Mock responses
items.5: Authentication Setup: Click the "Authentication" or "Auth" button in the "Try/Test" tab to set authentication values, which will be automatically included in all test requests

items.1: API Specification – How to write endpoints in the UI
items.2: Schema Management – Register reusable models
items.3: Mock API – Testing with the Try panel

apiSpec.title: API Specification
apiSpec.subtitle: This guide explains how to create and manage REST API specifications in the Ouroboros web UI.

items.1: Select "APIs" in the left sidebar and click the "New API" button.
items.2: Enter Path, Method, Summary, and Description.
items.3: Add items in Parameters, Request Body, and Responses sections or link Schemas.
items.4: Click the "Save" button in the top right to save the specification, and the Mock endpoint is immediately created.

manage.title: Specification Management
manage.desc: API Detail Page provides comprehensive information for each API specification. All information including request/response schemas, parameters, and metadata is organized in tabs for easy navigation.

items.overview: Overview Tab: View complete API specification including path, method, summary, description, and tags
items.request: Request Tab: Configure request parameters, headers, query parameters, and request body schema
items.response: Response Tab: Define response schemas for various status codes (200, 201, 400, 404, etc.)
items.try: API Try Tab: Execute API tests and check responses
items.validation: Validation Tab: Check validation status and mismatches between specification and implementation
items.code: Code Snippets: Generate code examples in various languages such as cURL, JavaScript, Python
items.export: Export: Export API documentation in Markdown or OpenAPI YAML format

items.1: Edit API details directly on the page
items.2: Reference reusable schemas in request/response bodies
items.3: Set development progress status and tags
items.4: Check validation status and apply changes

importExport.title: Import / Export
importExport.desc: You can import or export OpenAPI 3.1 YAML files using the "Import YAML" and "Export YAML" buttons in the top menu. When importing with existing specifications, the UI will automatically guide you through the merge results.

editor.title: Specification Editor
editor.desc: Specification Editor allows you to create and edit API specifications through an intuitive form-based editor. The editor provides a step-by-step workflow for defining all aspects of an API.

sections.title: Editor Sections
sections.basic: Basic Information: Define path, HTTP method (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, etc.), summary, and description

items.1: Add path parameters, query parameters, and headers
items.2: Define request body schema (reference existing schema or create inline)
items.3: Set content type (application/json, application/xml, etc.)

items.1: Add response definitions for each status code
items.2: Define response headers and body schema
items.3: Set response content type

sections.metadata: Metadata: Set development progress status (mock/completed), tags (none/implementing/bugfix), and validation status

items.1: Reference reusable schemas using {ref: "SchemaName"}
items.2: Auto-completion for schema names and field paths
items.3: Real-time validation for OpenAPI 3.1.0 compliance

websocket.title: WebSocket/STOMP API Specification
websocket.desc: Ouroboros supports the AsyncAPI 3.0.0 standard to create and manage WebSocket/STOMP API specifications.

items.1: Create Schema: Create schemas for message payloads in "WebSocket" → "Schemas" tab
items.2: Create Message: Define messages referencing schemas in "WebSocket" → "Messages" tab
items.3: Create Operation: Link channel address and messages in "WebSocket" → "receive" or "reply" tab
items.4: Enter channel address: Enter the full path including the application destination prefix (e.g., /app/chat/send)

items.1: Channel address: When writing channel addresses in specifications, you must enter the full path including the application destination prefix.
items.2: Annotations: Only methods with @MessageMapping and @SendTo annotations are scanned.
items.3: Specification storage location: All WebSocket/STOMP specifications are stored in src/main/resources/ouroboros/websocket/ourowebsocket.yml file.

tryFeature.title: Try Feature
tryFeature.subtitle: This guide explains how to track API execution and analyze down to the method level without additional infrastructure.

items.1: Default: Available immediately with in-memory storage without configuration
items.2: Trigger: Only requests with X-Ouroboros-Try: on header are tracked
items.3: Query: Query performance data using X-Ouroboros-Try-Id in response headers

items.1: Open the "API Try" tab on the API detail screen and enter parameters.
items.2: Clicking the "RUN" button automatically adds headers and executes the request.
items.3: Check execution time, status code, Mock data, etc. in the response panel.
items.4: You can query recent Try history again in the "TEST" panel on the right.

directRequest.desc: When calling with tools (HTTPie, Postman, etc.), add headers manually.
directRequest.note: Copy the Try ID from the response header and check details via REST API such as /ouro/tries/{tryId}.

tempo.title: Tempo Integration (Optional)

whenToUse.title: 💡 When to Use Tempo

items.1: Persistent trace storage (traces persist after application restart)
items.2: Advanced trace analysis features
items.3: Trace sharing across multiple application instances

whenToUse.note: For most use cases, in-memory storage is sufficient and no additional configuration is required.

tempo.desc: If persistent storage or advanced analysis is needed, you can optionally configure Grafana Tempo.

appConfig.title: Enable Tempo in Application Configuration
appConfig.code:
# Enable Tempo Integration (Ouroboros SDK uses TraceQL)
# If not set or set to false, in-memory storage is used by default
ouroboros.tempo.enabled=true
ouroboros.tempo.base-url=http://${TEMPO_HOST:localhost}:${TEMPO_UI_PORT:3200}
appConfig.note: If not set or set to false, in-memory storage is used by default.

otelConfig.title: OpenTelemetry Exporter Configuration
otelConfig.note: Note: This configuration is only required when using Tempo integration (ouroboros.tempo.enabled=true).
otelConfig.code:
# OpenTelemetry Exporter (App -> Tempo)
# Using HTTP protocol (port 4318)
management.tracing.enabled=true
management.otlp.tracing.endpoint=http://${TEMPO_HOST:localhost}:${TEMPO_HTTP_PORT:4318}/v1/traces
otelConfig.envNote: Note: ${TEMPO_HOST:localhost} and ${TEMPO_HTTP_PORT:4318} reference environment variables set in the .env file.

structure.title: Configuration File Structure
structure.code:
.
├─ docker-compose.yml      # Tempo container configuration
├─ tempo.yaml              # Tempo configuration file
├─ .env                    # Docker ↔ App sync variables (required)
├─ tempo-data/             # Local trace data storage folder (auto-generated)
└─ src/main/resources/application.properties  # Spring Boot app configuration

envFile.title: Create .env File
envFile.desc: Create a .env file in the project root (where docker-compose.yml is located).
envFile.code:
# ====== Docker ↔ App Sync Variables ======
# Tempo server address (Docker container name or localhost)
TEMPO_HOST=localhost

# Tempo ports (Docker Compose ↔ Spring Boot sync)
TEMPO_HTTP_PORT=4318  # OTLP HTTP (trace data transmission)
TEMPO_UI_PORT=3200    # Tempo UI / Query API
envFile.note: These variables are required for port/host synchronization between Docker Compose and Spring Boot.

noteItems.2: When running inside Docker network → TEMPO_HOST=tempo

dockerCompose.title: Docker Compose Configuration
dockerCompose.desc: Create a docker-compose.yml file in the project root.
dockerCompose.code:
services:
  tempo:
    image: grafana/tempo:2.6.1
    container_name: tempo
    ports:
      - "${TEMPO_HTTP_PORT:-4318}:4318"  # OTLP HTTP (trace data reception)
      - "${TEMPO_UI_PORT:-3200}:3200"    # Tempo UI / Query API
    command: ["-config.file=/etc/tempo/tempo.yaml"]
    volumes:
      - ./tempo.yaml:/etc/tempo/tempo.yaml:ro
      - ./tempo-data:/var/tempo
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-qO-", "http://localhost:3200/ready"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 10
    networks:
      - tempo-net

networks:
  tempo-net:
    driver: bridge
dockerCompose.note: Note: Only HTTP protocol is used, so gRPC port (4317) is not required.

tempoYaml.title: Tempo Configuration File
tempoYaml.desc: Create a tempo.yaml file in the project root:
tempoYaml.code:
server:
  http_listen_port: 3200

storage:
  trace:
    backend: local
    local:
      path: /var/tempo/traces

distributor:
  receivers:
    otlp:
      protocols:
        http:
          endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4318
tempoYaml.note: Note: Only HTTP protocol is used, so gRPC protocol configuration has been removed.

run.title: Run Tempo
run.code:
# Start Tempo container
docker compose up -d

# Verify execution
docker ps
docker logs tempo -f

gitignore.title: Gitignore Configuration (for Tempo)
gitignore.desc: Add the following items to your project's .gitignore file:
gitignore.code:
# ===== Ouroboros SDK Try Feature Related =====
# Tempo data directory
tempo-data/

# Environment variable files
.env
.env.local
.env.*.local

# Docker Compose override
docker-compose.override.yml

items.1: tempo.yaml: This file is a project configuration file and should be included in Git.
items.2: docker-compose.yml: This is a Docker Compose configuration file and should be included in Git.
items.3: tempo-data/: The Tempo data directory should not be included in Git.
items.4: .env: Environment variable files should not be included in Git.

schema.title: Schema Management
schema.subtitle: This guide explains how to create and use reusable data models (Schemas) in the web UI.

items.1: Select "Schemas" in the left sidebar.
items.2: Click the "New Schema" button and enter name and description.
items.3: Add fields in the Properties area and set type, required status, and Mock values.
items.4: When you save, the Schema is registered and can be referenced immediately when creating APIs.

items.1: Selecting a Schema from the list allows you to edit details in the right panel.
items.2: You can duplicate similar structures using "Duplicate" or delete using "Delete" when needed.
items.3: Schema names are immediately displayed in the $ref selection list in APIs.

mock.title: Mock Data
mock.desc: Each field can specify Mock expressions using DataFaker syntax in x-ouroboros-mock, which is used when checking Mock responses in the Try panel.

examples.title: Examples:

items.1: {{random.uuid}} - Generate UUID
items.2: {{name.fullName}} - Generate full name
items.3: {{internet.emailAddress}} - Generate email address

examples.note: Using DataFaker syntax allows you to automatically generate Mock data similar to real data.

websocket.title: Schema and Message for WebSocket
websocket.desc: You can define separate Schemas and Messages for WebSocket/STOMP API specification creation.
websocket.schemaDesc: Create schemas for WebSocket message payloads in "WebSocket" → "Schemas" tab. You can define fields and types the same way as REST API Schemas, and DataFaker syntax is also available.
websocket.messageDesc: Define Messages that reference previously created Schemas in "WebSocket" → "Messages" tab. Messages are used in WebSocket Operations.
websocket.note: Note: WebSocket Schemas and Messages are managed independently from REST API Schemas, and WebSocket specifications are stored in the ourowebsocket.yml file.
websocket.notePart1: Note: WebSocket Schemas and Messages are managed independently from REST API Schemas,

mockApi.title: Mock API
mockApi.subtitle: This guide explains how to check and use Mock responses in the web UI.

items.1: Select the "API Try" tab on the API detail screen.
items.2: Enter required Path/Query/Header values.
items.3: If there is a Request Body, modify the example JSON and click the "RUN" button.
items.4: You can immediately check Mock response body and headers in the "TEST" panel at the bottom right.

auth.title: Authentication Setup
auth.desc: You can configure authentication settings before testing APIs. Click the "Authentication" or "Auth" button to enter authentication information, which will be automatically included in all test requests.

response.title: Response Check
response.desc: Testing Screen allows you to test APIs and check Mock and actual responses, and also provides method-level performance tracking.

items.mock: Mock Response: Test with Mock data generated from specifications (useful for frontend development)
items.actual: Actual Response: Test with actual backend implementation
items.compare: Side-by-Side Comparison: Verify implementation accuracy by comparing Mock vs actual responses

features.2: Code Snippet generation feature allows you to generate code examples in various languages such as cURL, JavaScript, Python

websocket.desc: WebSocket/STOMP APIs can also test Mock responses the same way as REST APIs.

items.1: Select the "API Try" tab on the WebSocket Operation detail screen.
items.2: Enter message payload (Mock expressions defined in Schema are automatically filled).

openApiExtension.title: OpenAPI Extensions
openApiExtension.subtitle: This document summarizes Ouroboros custom extension fields and automatic correction rules.

operation.title: Operation-level Extensions

items.diff: x-ouroboros-diff: Difference between specification and implementation (none | request | response | endpoint | both)

diffItems.request: request: Difference in request parameters, headers, or body schema
diffItems.response: response: Difference in response status code, headers, or body schema
diffItems.endpoint: endpoint: Path and method do not match between specification and implementation
diffItems.both: both: Both request and response differ

operation.note: When you modify the specification, x-ouroboros-diff is automatically reset to none.

schema.title: Schema-level Extensions
schema.note: Ouroboros automatically adds missing Ouroboros extension fields and enhances specifications during validation.

implementationValidation.title: Implementation Validation
implementationValidation.subtitle: This guide explains how to manage and check specification and implementation progress status in the web UI.
implementationValidation.lombokWarning: If your project uses Lombok, you must include annotationProcessor 'org.projectlombok:lombok' in the build configuration. Without this setting, @ApiState metadata will not be generated and automatic validation will not work.
implementationValidation.websocketAnnotationNote: Only methods with @MessageMapping and @SendTo annotations are scanned

items.1: Progress values are automatically adjusted to "mock" or "completed" by the SDK comparing specification and implementation status.
items.2: Tags are also automatically updated based on scan results to show current implementation status (implementing, bugfix, etc.).
items.3: Changes are reflected in the list immediately after saving, so there is no need to manually manipulate progress.

status.title: Status Check
status.desc: You can see the progress status for each API at a glance in the list or detail screen, with badge colors displayed according to status.

items.mock: mock: Only Mock responses are provided
items.completed: completed: Endpoints with actual implementation completed

validation.title: Automatic Validation
validation.desc: Specifications created by users are automatically compared with OpenAPI scan results from the running application. When you save changes, the SDK synchronizes specifications and implementations and displays mismatches.

types.request: Request Validation: Compare request parameters, headers, body schema
types.response: Response Validation: Compare response status codes, headers, body schema
types.endpoint: Endpoint Validation: Check if path and method match between specification and implementation
types.both: Both: Both request and response differ from specification

features.1: Visual Diff Display: Accurately check differences between specification and implementation
features.2: One-Click Sync: Apply changes from code to specification with one click
features.3: Validation Status Badge: Display validation status for each endpoint (Valid/Invalid/Diff detected)
features.4: Detailed Reports: Check comprehensive validation reports for all endpoints
features.5: Filter by Status: Filter endpoints by validation status for quick review

workflow.1: Check validation results after code scanning
workflow.2: Review highlighted mismatch items in the interface
workflow.3: Apply changes to synchronize code and specification
workflow.4: Track validation status for each endpoint

validation.lombokNote: ⚠️ Important: For projects using Lombok, annotationProcessor 'org.projectlombok:lombok' configuration must be present for normal operation.

websocket.title: WebSocket/STOMP Validation
websocket.desc: WebSocket/STOMP APIs can also validate specifications and implementations the same way as REST APIs. Automatic validation is performed when code scanning is enabled through Springwolf.

types.channel: Channel Validation: Check if channel address matches between specification and implementation
types.message: Message Validation: Check if message payload schema matches between specification and implementation
types.operation: Operation Validation: Check if receive/reply Operations match between specification and implementation

requirements.1: Springwolf dependency addition and activation required
requirements.2: Only methods with @MessageMapping and @SendTo annotations are scanned
requirements.3: Channel addresses must be written as full paths including application destination prefix

knownIssues.title: Known Issues
knownIssues.subtitle: This document summarizes known issues and solutions to be aware of when using Ouroboros.

swagger.title: Conflict with Swagger UI
swagger.problem: Problem: If Swagger UI (springdoc-openapi) is installed in your project, it may conflict with Ouroboros.
swagger.cause: Cause: Conflicts occur when both Swagger UI and Ouroboros try to process OpenAPI schemas, causing path conflicts or empty configuration conflicts. Particularly, compatibility issues occur when springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui version is below 2.8.13 (e.g., 2.2.0).
swagger.solutionText: Upgrade springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui to version 2.8.13 or higher.

symptomItems.1: Errors occur when starting the application

solution.title: Solution
solution.desc: Upgrade springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui to version 2.8.13 or higher.

swagger.note: Note: Ouroboros provides its own web UI, so there is no need to use it together with Swagger UI. You can manage API specifications and use Mock server in Ouroboros web UI.

springBoot.title: Spring Boot 4.0.0 Not Supported
springBoot.problem: Problem: Ouroboros currently does not work with Spring Boot 4.0.0.
springBoot.supported: Supported Versions: Ouroboros only supports Spring Boot 3.5.7 or lower versions.
springBoot.cause: Cause: Package paths changed in Spring Boot 4.0.0, causing compatibility issues in parts where Ouroboros references existing paths.

solution.title: Solution
solution.desc: Downgrade Spring Boot version to 3.5.7 or lower, or wait until Spring Boot 4.0.0 support is added.

bugReport.title: Bug Report
bugReport.desc: If you discover other bugs or have improvements, please report them on GitHub Issues.

quickStart.title: Quick Start
quickStart.subtitle: This guide covers how to add Ouroboros to your project and get basic features working.

prerequisites.title: Prerequisites
prerequisites.lombokNote: If your project uses Lombok, the annotationProcessor 'org.projectlombok:lombok' configuration is required. Without it, @ApiState scanning will not work and automatic spec-implementation validation will not function.
prerequisites.swaggerNote: If using Swagger UI (springdoc-openapi) together, springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui version must be 2.8.13 or higher. Lower versions like 2.2.0 may cause conflicts. See known issues for details.

step1.title: Step 1: Installation
step1.basicDepsDesc: Adding only the basic dependencies allows you to use both REST API and WebSocket features.
step1.versionWarning: ⚠️ Do not use version 1.0.2 as it causes errors. Please use version 1.0.5.
step1.note1: The library internally includes spring-boot-starter-actuator and spring-boot-starter-aop.
step1.note2: Mock server and REST API controllers are registered via auto-configuration, so they can be used without additional setup.
step1.note3: If using Lombok, you must add annotationProcessor 'org.projectlombok:lombok' for @ApiState-based automatic scanning to work properly.

step2.title: Step 2: Configuration
step2.configDesc: You can add the following configuration to application.yml or application.properties:
step2.disableNote: If disabled, all controllers, filters, and auto-configuration will not be registered. (e.g., ouroboros.enabled=false)
step2.springwolfImportant: ⚠️ Important: The springwolf.enabled=false setting is required even when using REST API only. Without this setting, the application may fail to boot properly.
step2.websocketDesc: Configuration for WebSocket/STOMP API code scanning feature. WebSocket spec writing is available with just the base dependency.
step2.websocketItem1: For spec writing only: Set springwolf.enabled=false without adding Springwolf dependencies.
step2.websocketItem2: For code scanning: Add Springwolf dependencies and enable Springwolf.
step2.websocketItem3: Channel address: When writing channel addresses in specs, you must enter the full path including the application destination prefix. (e.g., /app/chat/send)
step2.websocketItem4: Annotations: Only methods with @MessageMapping and @SendTo annotations are scanned.
step2.option2: Option 2: Code Scanning and Spec Comparison (Springwolf Enabled)
step2.restConfigCode:
ouroboros:
  enabled: true  # Default: true
  server:
    url: http://localhost:8080
    description: Local Development Server

  # Method Tracing Configuration (Optional)
  # Only configure when internal method tracing is needed for Try feature
  method-tracing:
    enabled: true
    allowed-packages: your.package.name  # Specify package paths to trace

# Springwolf Configuration (Required)
# Set to false if using REST API only or if WebSocket code scanning is not needed
springwolf:
  enabled: false  # Required when not using WebSocket code scanning
step2.option1Code:
springwolf:
  enabled: false  # Disable Springwolf (spec writing only)
step2.option2Code:
springwolf:
  enabled: true
  docket:
    info:
      title: WebSocket API
      version: 1.0.0
      description: WebSocket API Description
    servers:
      websocket:
        host: localhost:8080
        protocol: ws
        description: WebSocket Server
    base-package: com.yourpackage  # Package path to scan for @MessageMapping

step3.title: Step 3: Run Application
step3.ideNote: Or run the Spring Boot application from your IDE.

step4.title: Step 4: Access Web UI
step4.desc: Open the following address in your browser:
step4.note: You can create and manage API specifications from the web UI.

step5.title: Step 5: Create Your First API Specification
step5.restDesc: Create REST API specifications in the web UI:

restSteps.1: Enter path, HTTP method, summary, etc.

step5.restNote: Once saved, Mock API is automatically generated and ready for testing.
step5.websocketDesc: You can create WebSocket/STOMP API specifications. AsyncAPI 3.0.0 standard is supported.

websocketSteps.1: Create Schema: Create schemas for message payloads in "WebSocket" → "Schemas" tab
websocketSteps.2: Create Message: Define messages referencing schemas in "WebSocket" → "Messages" tab
websocketSteps.3: Create Operation: Link channel address and messages in "WebSocket" → "receive" or "reply" tab
websocketSteps.4: Enter channel address: Include full path (e.g., /app/chat/send)

step5.websocketNote: Note: If you only need WebSocket spec writing, you don't need to add Springwolf dependencies. Configure Springwolf only when you need code scanning and spec comparison features.

step6.title: Step 6: Mock API Testing
step6.desc: If an endpoint is not implemented according to the specification or if @ApiState's progress is not completed, requests to that endpoint will automatically return Mock responses.

step7.title: Step 7: Using Try Feature
step7.desc: The Try feature tracks and records API request execution times. It is enabled by default with no additional configuration required, using in-memory storage to view results immediately.

webUiSteps.1: Select "API Try" tab on API detail screen
webUiSteps.3: Check execution history in result area and "TEST" panel

step7.methodTracingDesc: To trace down to method level, add the following configuration. (Not required for basic Try feature usage)
step7.methodTracingNote: For detailed settings, refer to Try Feature Guide and TRY_SETUP.md.
step7.websocketTryImportant: Important: To use Try feature with WebSocket specs, the message broker's /queue prefix must be enabled.
step7.websocketTryDesc: If access to /queue prefix is not allowed in message broker configuration, WebSocket Try feature may not work properly.
